items.title: Evidence-grounded large language models guide perovskite solar cell design and optimization
items.summary: Researchers created PSM-Bench, an 800‑question test, to assess large language models’ scientific reasoning for perovskite solar cell design, and launched OpenPerov to aid this work.
items.whyItMatters: It shows LLMs can help accelerate materials discovery, a key interest for tech‑savvy innovators.

items.title: TopoQuant: Topological Framework to Characterize Behavioral Shifts in Quantized Large Language Models
items.summary: TopoQuant uses topological data analysis to measure structural drift in quantized LLMs’ self-attention weights, beyond accuracy metrics.
items.whyItMatters: It helps engineers detect hidden behavioral changes after quantization, improving model reliability.

items.title: Autonomous Analysis of Thermoelectric Materials Big Data by Multi-Agentic AI and Construction of a Knowledge Base and Specialized AI
items.summary: The article describes a Multi‑Agentic AI system that analyzes experimental thermoelectric data, records decisions, and builds a traceable knowledge base.
items.whyItMatters: It enables faster, reproducible material discovery for tech‑savvy researchers.

items.title: XLA from the Trenches: Correctness on TPU Workloads at Scale
items.summary: The article discusses how aggressive optimizations in domain-specific compilers for TPUs can compromise correctness, risking numerical errors and memory corruption during large-scale training.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because correctness issues can invalidate expensive model training and affect deployment reliability.

items.title: Log-Driven Semantic Tuning for Mixed Integer Programming Solvers
items.summary: The paper proposes using solver logs to guide parameter tuning for mixed integer programming solvers, reducing costly black-box trials.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a faster, data-driven way to optimize solver performance, appealing to practitioners needing efficient MIP solutions.

items.title: Discovering Models for Experimental Quantum Systems with Agentic AI
items.summary: AI-driven model discovery helps analyze disorder in many-emitter quantum systems, improving understanding of cavity-QED experiments.
items.whyItMatters: It enables better design and control of quantum devices by tackling emitter inhomogeneity.

items.title: LM6-CastBench: A Geometry-Aware Simulation Dataset for Transient Thermal Prediction in LM6 Sand Casting
items.summary: A new dataset, LM6-CastBench, provides geometry-aware thermal simulations for predicting transient heat fields in LM6 aluminum sand castings.
items.whyItMatters: It enables faster, data-driven defect prediction for more efficient casting processes.

items.title: Enhancing Language Model Reasoning with Structured Multi-Level Modeling
items.summary: The paper proposes a structured multi-level modeling approach to improve inference-time reasoning in language models, mitigating plan drift in chain-of-thought methods.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a way to boost small LMs’ reasoning accuracy, benefiting developers needing reliable, efficient inference.

items.title: Learning from an Imitable Teacher: Competition Solution for the MetaFine Challenge
items.summary: Team Friday’s entry to the MetaFine Challenge demonstrates advanced fine‑grained manipulation, tackling tasks like precise peg insertion and part‑specific bottle grasping under varied perception conditions.
items.whyItMatters: It showcases progress in perception‑driven robotic manipulation, relevant for precision automation and AI‑guided assembly tasks.

items.title: ECG2Gene: Deep Learning-Based Germline Tumor Susceptibility Gene Risk Assessment Using Electrocardiograms
items.summary: ECG2Gene uses deep learning on 12‑lead ECGs to predict germline tumor susceptibility and future cancer risk.
items.whyItMatters: It could enable early cancer risk screening from routine heart tests.

items.title: Roz: A Taste Test for World Model Latents
items.summary: The paper evaluates whether state‑of‑the‑art latent dynamics world models truly capture physical properties like mass, friction, and deformation, finding they often miss these details.
items.whyItMatters: Tech‑savvy readers should know that strong image‑based performance may mask missing physics, impacting real‑world robot planning reliability.

items.title: Trail: Accurate Local Smart Home Control Using Decision Models
items.summary: Trail offers a fully local smart‑home framework that uses typed decision models to interpret natural‑language commands, avoiding cloud LLMs’ privacy risks and local SLMs’ errors.
items.whyItMatters: It gives tech‑savvy users secure, reliable voice control without cloud dependence.

items.title: Words Before Pixels: Selective Modality Routing for Vision-Language Model Unlearning
items.summary: Vision-language model (VLM) unlearning is often treated as an objective-design problem: given multimodal forget data, the goal is to optimize a loss that removes undesirable behavior while preserving retained capabilities. items.title: Sparse Autoencoder Attribution Graphs Are Decided at the Margin
items.summary: Attribution graphs over the features of sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are used to predict what an ablation does and are compared across training seeds. A TopK SAE keeps the largest preactivations at each token, and a feature's margin is its preactivation's distance to the cutoff. On five public TopK SAE pairs from three Pythia models, zeroing one feature moves a next layer feature across the cutoff…

items.title: Conversational Interaction for LLM-Based Clinical Text-to-SQL: A User Study with Healthcare Professionals
items.summary: Conversational text-to-SQL interfaces could give healthcare professionals natural-language access to electronic health record (EHR) data, but evidence for their real-world usability remains limited: prior evaluations have relied largely on curated benchmarks with fully specified questions or on simulated users. We report a user study in which 14 physicians who regularly work with EHR data used…

items.title: Editing the Goal: Per-Token SAE Steering and Its Depth Limits in π_0.5
items.summary: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) have recovered interpretable, causally relevant features in robot foundation models (RFMs) such as π_0.5 (arXiv:2603.19183, arXiv:2603.19233). SAE features on individual instruction tokens are less interpretable than timestep-pooled ones (arXiv:2603.19183), and whether they can redirect a robot's goal remains untested. items.title: Multi-Estimate Elicitation Does Not Uniformly Debias Language Model Judgments
items.summary: Does eliciting five weighted estimates within a single response change how a language model responds to information? Across anchoring, hindsight, base-rate, conjunction, and status-quo/default tasks, we compare direct numerical answers with a multi-estimate response format, contrasting source framings, explicitly random cues, and probability-consistency constraints. items.title: X-World 1.6: Building Controllable Virtual Cities with World Models
items.summary: Deploying generative world models for end-to-end closed-loop evaluation and policy learning requires precise scenario control, consistent observations, and sustained generation quality during extended interactions. This report presents X-World~1.6, advancing X-World~1.0 toward a more reliable and versatile driving simulator. The upgraded base model offers finer-grained control over traffic…

items.title: Do Orthogonality Constraints Help Language-Model Training Beyond Sphere Optimization?
items.summary: A growing body of work reports benefits from orthogonality constraints in fine-tuning large language models (LLMs). These results raise an open question: do orthogonality constraints also help LLM pre-training? We conduct a systematic empirical study of decoder-only LLM pre-training with models ranging from 360M to 3.1B parameters, trained on nearly 200B tokens. We examine fourteen variants of…

items.title: Saidzoda-Tajik-E5-Large: Fine-Tuning a 560M Embedder for Tajik Retrieval
items.summary: Finding the passage that answers a question is the first step of most practical systems built on documents, and for Tajik we found no openly described model for it. We present Saidzoda-Tajik-E5-Large, a Tajik text embedder built from multilingual-e5-large-instruct (560M parameters).
